method: Loaded JSON and existing batch.decode(packet) only; never load_packet. Complete original page ranges rendered using existing pdftoppm and inspected with view_image. All twenty extracted original text hashes independently match their frozen sources (SOURCE_FIXITY.json). Number/date/subject crosswalk and body/signature agree; numbers are not printed in the volume. These are source assessments, not reviews or approvals of unprovided proposed claims. No provisional NO is treated as lifecycle proof.
shared_limits: Held original existence and a mechanically empty missing list do not establish a first cessation or cutoff predicate. Frozen number-reference searches have incomplete historical/subject coverage: OFR catalog starts 1937, USC edition ends October 9, 2026, and eCFR covers stated 49 titles. No exhaustive independent historical-law search occurred. Original inventory below is substantive source inventory, not acceptance of machine clause segmentation. Raw FR actors have no usable raw locator supplied in the dossier, and the checked standard EO9830/EO8393 PDF paths were absent; no absent actor PDF is claimed read. EO1532 extracted file and packet-relative EO9830 overflow file were absent at their stated paths. Dossier excerpts are leads, not substitutes for full raw actor examination.

records.inventory: Sections1-6: constitute three-member inspection board; written classification and license issuance; applicant inquiry/examination and three-year licenses with suspension/revocation grounds; permanent-employment qualification/citizenship rule and existing officers' qualification; noncitizen licensing permission; limited amendment of Governor's December 8, 1905 pilot order.
records.effective_date_check: Signed October 2, 1909; no delayed effectiveness stated in original.
records.challenge: Three years is a term of each issued license, not a sunset three years after this EO. Board, examination and employment rules recur independently. Limited pilot amendment does not terminate EO1131.
unresolved_questions: What later law ends or continues each licensing, employment and board provision, and on what effective dates?
Read complete Governor's pilot order and intervening Canal law before attributing displacement; distinguish existing licenses and accrued proceedings from prospective rules.

records.inventory: Two textual additions to February 20, 1908 procedure, followed by full restatement: reasons, department approval, CSC reference and report to President; restrictions/exceptions on recommendations to Congress.
records.effective_date_check: Signed January 12, 1910; source contains no own sunset. Frozen EO9830 effective wording points to May 1, 1947, not its February 24 signing date, but actor raw examination remains incomplete.
records.challenge: Amendment creates continuing amended procedure; it is not spent upon insertion. EO9830 PartIII excerpt names number1153 and January12,1910, a later revocation lead only. Full overflow actor context is absent at packet-relative path; read only available preamble/PartIII portions of held EO9830 text, not complete actor raw pages.
unresolved_questions: Did any earlier statute or order alter or end recommendations/reporting restrictions before EO9830?
Obtain complete pinned actor raw access and test effective-date scope, independent commands and savings; no first end established by listing alone.

records.inventory: Articles1-6: legal-adviser/opinion/litigation/prosecution duties; subpoena and oath powers; information filing/verification; replacement criminal-procedure section138; peace-officer process execution and named officer classes, expressly cumulative; conflict repeal.
records.effective_date_check: Signed April 16, 1910; no expiration or delayed start stated.
records.challenge: Counsel duties do not exhaust subpoena, information, process or code-amendment provisions. Article5 expressly preserves existing execution-of-process law. A single whole paragraph machine scope cannot hide these distinct rules.
unresolved_questions: Trace first cessation/current predicate separately for duties, judicial powers and section138 through later Canal institutional/code changes.
Which existing proceedings and cumulative powers survive each change, under its actual savings and effective provisions?

records.inventory: Articles1-5: married woman's conveyance/mortgage requirements; retroactive validation of specified instruments; personal/private acknowledgment procedures and two certificate forms; domestic/foreign authorized acknowledging officials and certificates; specified Civil Code/conflict repeals with express prior-law instrument saving.
records.effective_date_check: Signed August 20, 1910; no separate delayed start or sunset stated.
records.challenge: Retroactive validation of old deeds is not the cessation of prospective acknowledgment rules. Article5 expressly protects deeds/instruments executed pursuant to prior law. Property titles and validity consequences must be distinguished from continuing regulatory force.
unresolved_questions: What later instrument changes each acknowledgment and conveyance rule and when?
Trace surviving validated titles and express savings without calling permanent consequences current regulatory commands or assuming their extinction.

records.inventory: Sections1-10: abolish district tax collector; transfer duties/deputies with bond-law preservation; superior tax liens and20% penalty; delinquency warrant, seizure/sale and accounting; personal-property redemption/title; government succession to forfeiture/redemption; real-estate tax deeds; transfer former municipal tax powers; conflict repeal and continuation of earlier proceedings/delinquencies; preserve senior officers' appointment/supervision powers.
records.effective_date_check: Signed October 4, 1910; no separate delayed start or end stated.
records.challenge: Abolition is only one component. Recurring collection, liens, accounting, redemption, title and deputy provisions are independent. Sections2,9,10 require express savings analysis; abolition cannot make the complete order spent at signing.
unresolved_questions: Trace each operative tax and office provision through subsequent Canal legislation/codes with exact effective dates.
Separate completed abolition and vested tax-sale titles from ongoing liabilities, saved proceedings and prospective administration.

records.inventory: Paragraph1 American-vessel deserter complaint/warrant/hearing and detention/delivery/cost rules; paragraph2 discharge for specified voyage/treatment conditions, wage/passage/employment relief, lien and log entries; paragraph3 treaty-conditioned foreign-consular deserter procedure, nationality exclusions, two-month arrest-based detention ceiling and criminal-case delay; paragraph4 effective wording.
records.effective_date_check: From and after May 6, 1911, the signing date, as paragraph4 states.
records.challenge: Two months runs from each arrest, not signing, and is not a sunset for this recurring regime. Treaty conditions and domestic/foreign procedures differ; wages, liens and records are additional operative consequences.
unresolved_questions: What later Canal/seamen law or treaty change reaches each rule and on what date?
Determine first cessation of prospective arrest powers separately from pending cases, discharge relief and liens; no universal two-month ending is supported.

records.inventory: SectionsI-VIII: ten-cent-per-litre distillation tax; licensing/bond or deposit; meter measurement and withholding license; bulk-sale permission; misdemeanors/penalties; implementing regulations; conflict repeal; delayed effective date.
records.effective_date_check: Original says thirty days from May13,1911. Complete EO1372 at PDF250/printed237 expressly changes effectiveness to August13,1911; this is a start-date amendment, not cessation.
records.challenge: Frozen EO1532 OCR context permits approved alternative measurement and bars operation of stills from January1,1913 with a new offense. It does not on its face settle collection of accrued tax, bonds/deposits, existing penalties or every EO1353 rule. EO1532 actual text file was absent at its stated path, and no raw page was supplied/read; no actor approval follows from the excerpt.
unresolved_questions: Inspect complete pinned EO1532 raw source and distinguish meter amendment from cessation of operating rights.
Trace tax liabilities/security/enforcement and later law; do not treat January1,1913 ban as automatic whole-order end or original thirty-day term as expiration.

records.inventory: Sole permission to waive United States citizenship for Isthmus job applicants under Civil Service Commission regulations.
records.effective_date_check: Signed December8,1904; no own-term end. EO9830 lead points to May1,1947 effective preamble, requiring full actor verification rather than signing-date substitution.
records.challenge: Waiver is a recurring regulatory permission, not a performed individual appointment. Held PartIII excerpt names No.283 of December8,1904, but locating a later express revocation does not establish first cessation. Referenced complete actor overflow is absent packet-relative; actor raw not examined.
unresolved_questions: Did intervening Canal employment law, civil-service rules or departmental regulations end or change this waiver earlier?
Close pre1937/subject-law coverage, examine full actor/savings and preserve already valid appointments as consequences separate from fresh waiver authority.

records.inventory: Exception from Civil-Service RuleXII clause2 removal procedure for Isthmus personnel, with independent duty to record reasons and furnish copies/originals to CSC upon request.
records.effective_date_check: Signed September8,1905; no own sunset.
records.challenge: Complete frozen EO8393 text concerns Makua land and the Governor of Hawaii's No.351 dated January23,1929. Different issuing authority, date and subject: no ending of presidential EO351. Actor raw was not supplied/visually examined, so this is a text-based identity challenge, not raw actor approval.
unresolved_questions: Trace actual later removal/procedural law and the separate record-production obligation.
What establishes the first cessation or cutoff predicate, including accrued requests/records, after excluding this false number-match lead?

records.inventory: Sole permission to hold the quarterly session for January1,1906 at Commission offices in Washington instead of Governor's office on Isthmus; reasons concern engineers' report and travel.
records.effective_date_check: Signed December7,1905; January1 is the identified session, not a stated adjournment or end date.
records.challenge: Venue permission covers a session. Parent EO317A expressly allows sessions to continue as public business requires (complete PDF46-49 read). No minutes/performance/adjournment proof is supplied. EO506 concerns a different October/November1906 session; it does not expressly repeal this January venue permission. January2 cannot simply be inferred as whole-case cessation.
unresolved_questions: When did the authorized January session actually conclude, or what legal instrument extinguished its special permission?

Distinguish a one-session venue permission from recurring schedule, a day's fresh commencement authority, and continuing validity of a convened session; assess intervening changes using adequate source coverage.

records.inventory: Sole permission for permanent appointment of Anna F. McCormick to an ICC office position where temporarily employed.
records.effective_date_check: Signed December18,1905; no fixed exercise deadline or automatic cessation stated.
records.challenge: May be permanently appointed is permission, not an appointment or proof it was exercised. Temporary employment recital does not establish permanent appointment, first exhaustion, death or later revocation.
unresolved_questions: Obtain exact personnel appointment/declination or other cessation evidence and its date.
Bound earlier/later legal changes and distinguish subsequent service/pay consequences from unexercised appointing permission.

records.inventory: Sole permission for permanent appointment of Ralph Whitman as Engineer Draftsman in ICC office where temporarily employed.
records.effective_date_check: Signed January8,1906; no sunset or exercise deadline stated.
records.challenge: Permanent appointment is authorized but not accomplished by the wording. Neither assumed prompt personnel action nor elapsed century supplies a first end.
unresolved_questions: What personnel or legal source establishes actual exercise or other first cessation and its date?
Trace any remaining authority and consequences separately, with adequate later search beyond number references.

records.inventory: Clarifying/amending expense allowances for chairman while away from Washington and governor/chief engineer while away from Isthmus on official business; express retroactive effectiveness.
records.effective_date_check: Signed March26,1906, expressly effective February26,1906 (parent EO418). Complete parent PDF83 and actor EO474 PDF86 read visually.
records.challenge: EO474 June30,1906 repeats the same expense entitlement and revokes conflicting orders only. Identical allowance is not established conflict and does not by itself terminate EO430. Amendment/interpretation continues in the parent scheme; do not substitute signing for retroactive effective date.
unresolved_questions: Locate a later instrument that actually extinguishes or replaces this allowance, testing precise scope and date.
Separate prospective entitlement and reimbursement of accrued expenses; address offices/personnel changes and earlier candidates rather than declaring June30 wholesale revocation.

records.inventory: Sole permission to transfer John E. Kidwell, accountant/pay-clerk at stated Isthmian salary, to a classified clerical United States position.
records.effective_date_check: Signed February21,1907; salary recital is not a term or cessation date.
records.challenge: Permission to transfer does not show transfer actually occurred. No appointment/transfer record or alternative terminating source appears in frozen evidence.
unresolved_questions: When, if ever, was the authorized transfer effected, or when was the permission otherwise ended?
Confirm exact person/position and distinguish continuing transferred employment from exhaustion of one transfer permission.

records.inventory: Ten paragraphs covering district boundaries; tax collector appointments/duties/records/bonds; tax liens/appeals/equalization; district judges and monthly conference; public works; district accounts and rent earmarks; ordinance authority; municipal-office abolition; officer appointments/salaries; inconsistent-law modification/repeal.
records.effective_date_check: Signed March13,1907, expressly effective April15,1907. Complete EO1250 PDF222-224 visually read as actor.
records.challenge: EO1250 abolishes the paragraph2 district-tax-collector office and reallocates duties; it does not expressly repeal all district boundaries, judges, public works, rent earmarks or ordinance powers. Its conflict clause and saved earlier proceedings require provision-by-provision analysis. One later partial office abolition cannot end whole EO586.
unresolved_questions: Determine which EO586 provisions conflict with EO1250 and which continue, including liens, accounts, earmarks and prior proceedings.
Trace each remaining provision to first cessation/current predicate through later institutional/code changes; preserve April15 start distinct from March13 signature.

records.inventory: Sole permission for W. P. Armstrong, ICC law clerk at $2400, to transfer to another competitive position at salary no greater than $2500 without transfer-rule limits.
records.effective_date_check: Signed March26,1907; annual salary amounts are not duration limits.
records.challenge: A salary-capped transfer exception does not establish a transfer, chosen job or exhaustion date. No own sunset or performance evidence appears.
unresolved_questions: What exact personnel record establishes use or cessation of this exception, and when?
Rule out material intervening changes and separate one-use permission from later employment consequences.

records.inventory: Four paragraphs: retroactive validation of specified marriages; prospective celebrant authority/license/age/impediment requirements; return/registration and $2 fee; misdemeanor for violating officers/ministers.
records.effective_date_check: Signed May31,1907; expressly effective June1,1907.
records.challenge: Validation of past marriages is distinct from continuing licensing, recording, fee and penal rules. It cannot make the complete order exhausted on June1 or prove that its authority remains current merely because old marriages remain valid.
unresolved_questions: Trace later marriage and Canal law for each prospective rule and any savings/effective dates.
Separate validated marital status/records/accrued liability from current rulemaking and enforcement; no first end/current predicate is established.

records.inventory: Adds Penal Code section293-a with five categories (vagrancy, begging, unauthorized presence/peddling, intoxication, disorderly conduct) and common misdemeanor/fine/imprisonment penalty.
records.effective_date_check: Signed January9,1908; amendment expressly effective January15,1908.
records.challenge: This is a continuing code amendment. Thirty days is a maximum sentence, not a thirty-day lifespan for the order. Neither insertion nor individual sentence completion ends the recurring offenses.
unresolved_questions: Identify subsequent code/judicial/institutional changes reaching each offense and penalty, with effective dates.
Assess accrued prosecutions/savings separately from prospective enforcement; original alone cannot establish whole lifecycle.

records.inventory: Four paragraphs: sale authority after six-month unclaimed period and three-week advertisement; perishable-property judicial route; inspection and four-week mailed notice where address indicated; net sale residue held three years, payable on demand then to public-school fund if unclaimed.
records.effective_date_check: Signed January9,1908; no order-level sunset stated.
records.challenge: Six months, three weeks, four weeks and three years run on particular property, notice, sale and residue facts, not from signing. Recurring sale regime and duties to hold/pay/transfer residue are separate commands. A three-year own-term whole-order end would be false.
unresolved_questions: Trace the sale regime and each residual-money obligation through later law with exact effective and savings rules.
What evidence distinguishes accrued property interests and pending custody duties from ceased prospective authority? No transaction dates or universal end are supplied.

records.inventory: Amends section22 of Act1: three judicial circuits, assigning Ancon to first, Emperador/Gorgona to second and Cristobal to third.
records.effective_date_check: Signed January9,1908; no separate delayed start or sunset stated.
records.challenge: A substituted jurisdictional rule continues as amended; it is not spent when the text is inserted or boundaries first recognized. No held ending/current-law evidence traces the circuit arrangement beyond original.
unresolved_questions: Read relevant parent Act1 and subsequent judicial/territorial reorganizations to establish first displacement of each circuit assignment.
Examine effective dates and pending-case/jurisdiction savings rather than inferring an end from later institutional history.
